name: Moss olive
lede: Moss olive is an xkcd survey name pairing two plant colors, the green of woodland moss and the duller yellow-green of olive.

sections.title: Two plants in one name
sections.body:
Our only recorded source for this exact name is the 2010 xkcd color survey, which asked thousands of people to name colors from swatches [1]. The name pairs two plant words rather than one: the green of woodland moss and the duller, yellow-green of an unripe or cured olive [1]. In the ISCC-NBS 1955 system the nearest block is "deep yellow green", a wider 8.3 units away than most of our matches, meaning no official dictionary entry sits very close [2]. In Munsell terms it reads about 5.1GY 4.8/6.6 [2].

Its nearest siblings in our data are plain [[moss]], which is lighter and less yellow, and [[olive]] itself, which is duller and greyer [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 55 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.2 percent, as photographed [3]. The earliest dated match is Andrea del Sarto's 1512 *Archangel Raphael with Tobias, St. Laurentius and the donor Leonardo di Lorenzo Morelli*, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. Its clearest peak is the 1890s, at close to three times the archive's overall rate [3]. [[painter:georges-seurat|Georges Seurat]] used it far more than most painters, at about 32 times the baseline rate, including in a 1883 study for *[[painting:nga-164966|Bathers at Asnières]]* [3]. On the same canvases it most often keeps company with [[olive]] and [[moss]], exactly the two plants in its own name [3]. These counts are computed color matches on photographs of aged, varnished paintings, not pigment identifications [3].
